manufacturer_data.description: Procter & Gamble (SIG-assigned 220). The advertisement carries the ID little-endian, so the wire bytes read `DC 00` — this field is the DECODED value, which is what a scanner compares against, not the bytes in advertisement order. Both device classes advertise under it: brush payloads are 15 bytes (the app accepts >= 5), chargers >= 10.

device.name: Oral-B iO Smart Brush
device.notes:
Extracted by static analysis of the official Oral-B Android app.
Uses A0F0XXXX-5047-4D53-8208-4F72616C2D42 UUID scheme where XXXX is a
16-bit short UUID. Suffix "4F72616C2D42" decodes to "Oral-B" in ASCII.
Manufacturer ID 0x00DC (220) = Procter & Gamble; the advertisement carries
it little-endian, so the wire bytes read DC 00.
Protocol versions V001 through V009 across brush generations.
Discovery uses manufacturer-specific advertisement data (app filters:
brush >= 5 bytes, charger >= 10; the full brush advertisement is 15 bytes).
Two device classes: Brush (FFxx UUIDs) and Charger (3Cxx UUIDs).
Supports OTA firmware updates via dedicated characteristic set. P&G's
official firmware host fw.iot-dev.alchemy.codes (hardcoded in the app's
own strings) serves unauthenticated RSA-signed update manifests for model
bytes 0x0031 (SONOS IO), 0x0034 (iO4), 0x0035 (iO5) and 0x0036 (E-Platform
= iO6-iO10): E-Platform/iO4/iO5 images are Silicon Labs Gecko Bootloader
GBL files, legacy SONOS images are TI CC2640 binaries; current firmware is
E-Platform V82 and iO4/iO5 V36; the legacy SONOS firmware train tops
out at V50. China is served from a separate S3 host
(email-assets-271825783008-cn-north-1.s3.cn-north-1.amazonaws.com.cn).

Transport parameters (app v10.8.0 BLE SDK): the app negotiates a
515-byte MTU on connect, requests CONNECTION_PRIORITY_HIGH (50 ms
latency) for active sessions, and serializes commands per UUID — writes
to the same characteristic are queued, different characteristics
interleave (RxJava command queue). Session/history data uses FF29 in a
write-then-notify pattern with timestamp-based sync.

credentials.notes: BLE-only; no WiFi passphrase is transferred. The P&G account credential is held by the app, not by the brush. The link is unauthenticated, so brushing data is readable by anyone in range.

factory_reset.description: Three different resets that people conflate because the vendor calls them all a reset. Pick by what actually needs clearing: brushing modes and preferences (app), a handle that has stopped responding (power button), or a smart charger that has lost its head (iOsense). Bluetooth is switched OFF from the display models' settings menu rather than by any of them, which is the thing to reach for when the goal is simply to stop a handle talking to a phone.
factory_reset.effect: Returns the handle to its default settings. What that includes varies by route and by model — the app's reset covers brush settings, the handle-button reset covers the handle, and the iOsense charger's reset covers the charger's own state.

methods.description: Connect over GATT to a brush (FFxx UUIDs) or its charger (3Cxx UUIDs) and read state directly. No pairing or account is involved.

steps.action: Switch the brush on, or seat it on its charger, so it advertises.
Scan for manufacturer-specific advertisement data under manufacturer ID 0x00DC. The app's brush filter needs at least 5 payload bytes (charger filter 10); the full brush advertisement is 15 bytes.
Connect over GATT and discover the A0F0xxxx-5047-4D53-8208-4F72616C2D42 services.
Read the protocol version characteristic to select the right command set — generations differ across V001 to V009.
steps.expect: A version string in the V001-V009 range.

setup.notes:
The brush needs no provisioning. It advertises manufacturer-specific data under P&G's manufacturer ID (0x00DC) whenever it is switched on, and exposes its state and control characteristics to any client that connects. The Oral-B app's account is for storing brushing history in P&G's cloud; the brush is not bound to it.
Confidence is medium: the UUID scheme and device classes are recovered from the vendor app, but the connect flow has not been exercised against hardware here. Note that discovery is by manufacturer data, not by service UUID — a scanner filtering on services will not see the brush.

rejoin.notes: The brush joins no network and holds no bond, so any client may connect once the previous one disconnects.

evidence.captured_implementation: thomasgregg/oralb-ha at c0910404ab3f4dffffcf6c3eb994a030d63f7306, covering an iO Series 10 with iO Sense on firmware 0.3.4. Its 488 tests passed. This is independent upstream capture evidence, not a physical test performed by this project.
evidence.follow_up: Reviewed 2026-11-06: corrected charger service and advertisement map, native read-only command grammar, charger status bits, length-gated FF05, retained-session FF29, ServiceDataA/B and V008+ SonosMetadata.
remaining_unknowns: Wi-Fi provisioning credential payloads and sequencing, charger durable upload queue enumeration, and firmware-container decryption
Protocol-6 FF29 layout, current/capacity units in ServiceDataA/B, and physical meaning of the second drive-target word
Hardware confirmation across other brush and charger firmware generations

dfu_mode.notes: No update-mode name, address or advertisement is recorded.

enter.notes: The update runs over vendor characteristics inside the one brush service a0f0ff00-…: OTACommand a0f0ff81 (write), OTAPayLoad a0f0ff82 (write), OTAVerify a0f0ff83 (read), OTAState a0f0ff84 (notify) and OTATransferSize a0f0ff85 (read). The command bytes that start an update are not recorded in this spec; MatrixEditor/oralb-io ships a working OTA client.

image.format: Silicon Labs Gecko Bootloader GBL (E-Platform, iO4, iO5); TI CC2640 binary (legacy SONOS).
image.notes: P&G's firmware host https://fw.iot-dev.alchemy.codes serves update manifests without authentication for model bytes 0x0031 (SONOS IO), 0x0034 (iO4), 0x0035 (iO5) and 0x0036 (E-Platform = iO6-iO10); China uses a separate S3 host (device.notes). The manifests are RSA-signed, and MatrixEditor/oralb-io ships the P&G public key that verifies them — that is the app's check. Whether the brush's own bootloader verifies the image (a GBL can carry an ECDSA signature and AES encryption) is not established.

dfu.notes: A vendor protocol carrying another stack's image: the GBL files are Silicon Labs format but travel over P&G's own characteristics, not the Silicon Labs OTA service. dfu.services is omitted because the OTA characteristics share a0f0ff00 with every ordinary brush characteristic; a GATT explorer should treat a0f0ff81-a0f0ff85 as the update path and never write them.

charger_advertisement.notes: Offsets are in the complete manufacturer AD structure. The 14-byte manufacturer value starts at full-packet offset 4. The vendor filter only requires length >9, but its builder reads through byte 17, so a robust parser requires all 18 bytes before decoding every field. Advertisements contain availability, not timer, pressure, zone, score or session data.

charger_bridge.boundaries: These native IDs are read-only observations, not permission for POST/EXECUTE. Wi-Fi provisioning credential sequencing, durable upload queue enumeration and firmware-container decryption are unknown. The charger is an outbound network client, not an inbound HTTP/HTTPS/SSH/ MQTT management API; authenticated vendor upload is not bypassed.

brush_passthrough_read.example: 08 ff 01 00 reads FF08; finish with e0 on 3C00
brush_passthrough_read.returned_data: 37 c1 uuid_lsb uuid_msb operation success length data…

charger_bridge.serialization: One complete transaction at a time; the tested charger rejects batched records. The charger forwards brush reads only while it owns the single brush connection.
charger_bridge.transaction: 3C00 [operation, command]; optional 3C02 payload; 3C00 e0; validate 3C03 [command, operation, result] with result 01 before using returned 3C01 data

characteristics.description: Current device state. State enum (from the app's device-state model): 0=UNKNOWN, 1=INIT, 2=IDLE, 3=RUN, 4=CHARGE, 5=SETUP, 6=FLIGHT_MENU, 7=CHARGE_FORBIDDEN, 8=PRE_RUN, 9=PAUSE, 10=POST_BRUSHING_STATISTICS, 113=FINAL_TEST, 114=PCB_TEST, 115=SLEEP, 116=TRANSPORT, 117=CALIBRATION_TEST. Plus SubState flags: -1=UNKNOWN, 0=TRANSPORT_DISABLED_DEACTIVATE_TIMER_DISABLED, 1=TRANSPORT_ENABLED_DEACTIVATE_TIMER_DISABLED, 3=TRANSPORT_ENABLED_DEACTIVATE_TIMER_ENABLED. Advertising byte 7 carries the same State value.

characteristics.name: BatteryLevel
characteristics.notes: Length-gated, little-endian battery record. The older one-byte percentage still works. Protocol 6 introduced remaining runtime; protocol 8 added the electrical fields. Protocol 6 treats zero runtime as unavailable, while later versions can return a genuine zero. Runtime 0xffff is unavailable; current -1 is unavailable. Do not decode absent electrical fields from a shorter record.

characteristics.notes: Retained latest-session summary, also readable through the charger's 0x37 passthrough. Protocol 7/8 uses the 21-byte layout in protocol_details.retained_session_ff29; protocol 6 differs. The captured direct client reads it after session settlement without an FF21 control command.

services.name: Oral-B iO Brush Service
services.notes: Brush service. The iO Sense charger has its own recovered service, a0f03e00-5047-4d53-8208-4f72616c2d42, declared separately below; its 3Cxx characteristics do not belong in this brush service. Older (pre-iO) brushes additionally expose FF01 DeviceID, FF02 DeviceInfo, FF03 UserID and FF2A (purpose unknown), per MatrixEditor/oralb-io and Bluetooth-Devices/oralb-ble; app v10 does not reference them.

characteristics.name: Charger command header and transaction delimiter
characteristics.notes: Carries the [operation, command] header and final e0 delimiter. The captured implementation serializes one complete transaction at a time.

characteristics.name: Charger returned data
characteristics.notes: Returned data is [command, operation, payload…]. A passthrough brush read returns 37 c1 uuid_lsb uuid_msb operation success length data….

characteristics.name: Charger command payload
characteristics.notes: Payload for the command named by the 3C00 header. A brush characteristic read uses uuid_lsb uuid_msb 01 00, then e0 on 3C00.

characteristics.name: Charger command status
characteristics.notes: Status is [command, operation, result], with 01 observed for success. Validate this before accepting returned data.

services.name: Oral-B iO Sense charger service
services.notes: Independently captured charger service, separate from the brush service. Protocol-2 headers are [operation, command]: GET c0, POST c1, EXECUTE c2. Every transaction ends with e0 on 3C00. Use the exact sequence in protocol_details.charger_bridge rather than issuing an isolated header.
